title: Perovskite solar cell stability
abstract: Perovskite solar cells have reached high power conversion efficiencies, but their long-term stability under humidity, heat and continuous illumination remains a barrier to commercial use. Here we introduce a two-dimensional capping layer that passivates surface defects and blocks moisture ingress. Devices retained most of their initial efficiency after one thousand hours of operation at elevated temperature. X-ray diffraction and photoluminescence measurements show reduced ion migration and suppressed non-radiative recombination at the interface.

title: CRISPR screen in tumour cells
abstract: We performed a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screen in human cancer cell lines to identify genes required for survival under nutrient stress. Several metabolic enzymes and transcription factors were found to be essential only when glucose was limited. Validation experiments using individual guide RNAs confirmed reduced proliferation and altered mitochondrial respiration. These results reveal protein targets that may be exploited to sensitise tumours to metabolic inhibitors in future therapeutic strategies.

title: Neutron star merger simulation
abstract: We present numerical relativity simulations of binary neutron star mergers using a range of nuclear equations of state. The gravitational wave signal, ejected mass and remnant lifetime are computed for different mass ratios. We find that stiffer equations of state produce longer-lived remnants and brighter electromagnetic counterparts. Comparison with detector sensitivity curves indicates that the post-merger oscillation frequency could constrain the high-density behaviour of nuclear matter.

title: Soil carbon under warming
abstract: Soils store more carbon than the atmosphere and vegetation combined, yet their response to climate warming is uncertain. In a ten-year field experiment we heated forest plots by four degrees and measured soil respiration, microbial biomass and enzyme activity. Respiration rose sharply during the first years and then declined as labile carbon pools were depleted. Isotopic analysis indicates that microbial community shifts, not only temperature, control the long-term carbon balance.

title: Transition metal catalysis for hydrogenation
abstract: We report a nickel-based molecular catalyst for the selective hydrogenation of unsaturated organic compounds under mild conditions. Kinetic experiments and density functional theory calculations suggest a mechanism involving heterolytic cleavage of hydrogen at the metal centre. The catalyst tolerates a wide range of functional groups and can be recycled several times without loss of activity. Spectroscopic characterisation of reaction intermediates supports the proposed catalytic cycle.

title: Supply chain resilience and firm performance
abstract: This study investigates how supply chain resilience influences financial performance in manufacturing firms. Using survey and archival data from several hundred companies, we show that supplier diversification and inventory flexibility raise profitability during periods of disruption. Management commitment and information sharing with customers strengthen the effect. The findings suggest that managers should invest in redundancy and visibility across the supply network to protect revenue and maintain competitive advantage.

title: Brand loyalty in e-commerce
abstract: We examine how perceived service quality and personalised marketing affect customer loyalty in online retail. A structural equation model based on data from consumers of major e-commerce platforms indicates that trust and satisfaction mediate the relationship between pricing strategy and repurchase intention. Loyalty programmes increase customer lifetime value, but their impact is weaker among price-sensitive shoppers. The results offer guidance for firms designing digital marketing and retention strategies.

title: Board diversity and shareholder returns
abstract: This paper analyses the relationship between corporate board composition and stock market performance for listed companies. Using panel data over fifteen years, we find that boards with greater diversity of experience are associated with lower earnings volatility and higher returns on equity. Institutional investors respond positively to governance reforms. We discuss implications for executive compensation, risk management and investor relations.

title: Startup funding and venture capital
abstract: Early-stage ventures face substantial barriers in raising capital. We study how founder characteristics, business model novelty and investor networks shape the likelihood of securing venture capital funding. Analysis of a large dataset of startups shows that experienced entrepreneurs and strong syndicate partners increase valuation at the first funding round. Entrepreneurs who pivot their strategy too frequently, however, receive lower offers from investors.

title: Employee engagement and organisational productivity
abstract: Organisations increasingly rely on employee engagement initiatives to improve productivity and reduce turnover. In this study of service companies, we show that transformational leadership and clear performance feedback raise engagement, which in turn increases sales per employee. Remote work arrangements moderate these effects. Human resource managers can use these insights to design incentive systems and improve workforce retention.

title: Social media and political participation
abstract: This article examines how social media use relates to political participation among young adults. Drawing on a national survey, we find that exposure to political content online increases voting intention and protest activity, but only when users also discuss politics with peers offline. Differences by education and income suggest that digital platforms may deepen existing inequalities in civic engagement. We discuss implications for democratic institutions and media policy.
label: Social Science

title: Teacher expectations and student achievement
abstract: We investigate how teacher expectations shape student outcomes in secondary schools. A longitudinal study of classrooms shows that students from disadvantaged backgrounds who receive higher expectations from teachers achieve better grades and are more likely to continue to higher education. Qualitative interviews reveal that supportive classroom culture and parental involvement strengthen this relationship. The findings highlight the role of pedagogy and school policy in reducing educational inequality.
label: Social Science

title: Migration and community identity
abstract: Using ethnographic fieldwork in two urban neighbourhoods, this study explores how migrants negotiate belonging and cultural identity. Residents describe daily interactions, language use and religious practice as ways of building solidarity while facing discrimination. The analysis shows that local community organisations play a central role in social integration. We argue that policies on migration should consider the lived experience of families and the gendered division of care work.
label: Social Science

title: Urban poverty and family wellbeing
abstract: This paper explores the effects of persistent poverty on families living in large cities. Interviews and household surveys show that unstable housing, low wages and limited access to public services undermine child development and mental wellbeing. Social support networks and welfare programmes partly buffer these effects. The study contributes to sociological debates on inequality, social mobility and the role of the state.
label: Social Science

title: Gender norms and household labour
abstract: We analyse how gender norms shape the division of unpaid household work in dual-earner couples across several countries. Cross-national survey data indicate that women continue to perform a larger share of domestic and care tasks, even when they work full-time. Cultural attitudes and family policy, such as parental leave design, explain much of the variation. The results inform debates on gender equality and social policy reform.
